Edit the attached SELECTED two-line hand-lettered logo for Little Stone Still Here. The user likes this exact direction and asks for polishing it into their logo. Treat this as careful typographic finishing, NOT redesign.

Retain the original overall feel and letter anatomy. The two lines remain one centered, intimate inscription. Do not substitute a computer font, generic cursive, brush-script font, geometric sans or decorative calligraphy. Do not make it look like a typed font.

REFINE only these concrete issues:
1. In stone, correct the N-like character to a clearly LOWERCASE n: a straight or gently leaning stem followed by one controlled arch/shoulder, coherent with the h and r. No uppercase diagonal N.
2. Make r in here clearly read as lowercase r with a concise shoulder; do not let it read as v. Keep all letters unmistakable. There are TWO t letters in little, TWO l letters in still.

No brittle hairlines that vanish when moderately reduced.
6. Match the perceived ink weight of both lines; first-line l and t strokes must not overpower second-line text. Calm, poised, personal, restrained.

Render this ONE polished wordmark in pure flat white ink on pure flat black, no gradients, shadows, texture, bevels or lighting.
